q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM ( SELECT VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ) F ORDER BY 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM ( SELECT VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ) F ORDER BY 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (3, 103, 201, '2023-01-02');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the difference in the GROUP BY clauses. Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups only by VIEW_DATE. This difference can lead to different results when the same VIEWER_ID has multiple VIEW_DATE entries.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have the same VIEWER_ID with multiple VIEW_DATE entries to trigger the difference between Q1 and Q2.
